results.title: Daytona Pricing Explained: Rates, Tiers, and Workload Costs | Beam
results.author: Eli Mernit
highlights:
Eli Mernit· November 6, 2026· 11 min read

Daytona pricing is pay-as-you-go with no plan fee. A running sandbox costs $0.0504 per vCPU-hour and $0.0162 per GiB-hour of memory, billed per second, and disk costs $0.000108 per GiB-hour after the first 5 GiB. New accounts get $200 in free compute without a credit card. Below are the rate card, the tier limits, what typical workloads cost, and how Daytona compares with E2B, Modal and Beam.

...

## Daytona GPU pricing

Daytona GPU sandboxes cost from $0.57 per GPU-hour for a spot RTX 4090 to $6.25 for an on-demand B200 or B300, and the sandbox's vCPU and memory may be billed on top. Each sandbox takes up to 8 GPUs. GPU sandboxes are ephemeral and use a separate GPU quota, so they don't draw on the tier's CPU pool.

| GPU | Spot, per GPU-hour | On-demand, per GPU-hour |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA RTX 4090 | $0.57 | $0.99 |
| NVIDIA RTX 5090 | $0.74 | $1.29 |
| NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 | $1.74 | $3.03 |
| NVIDIA H100 | $2.27 | $3.95 |
| NVIDIA H200 | $2.61 | $4.54 |
| AMD MI355X | $3.44 | $5.99 |
| NVIDIA B200 | $3.59 | $6.25 |
| NVIDIA B300 | $4.08 | $6.25 |

### What a Daytona GPU sandbox costs with CPU and memory

The GPU rate may not be the whole bill. Daytona's billing docs list vCPU, memory and disk as billed for GPU sandboxes while they run, the same as for CPU sandboxes, and the pricing page doesn't say the GPU rate includes them. What that adds depends on how you create the sandbox:

| How the sandbox is created | vCPU / RAM / disk | Added per hour at standard rates |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create request with no resources set | 16 / 192 GiB / 512 GiB | $3.97 |
| From the default daytona-gpu snapshot | 1 / 1 GiB / 1 GiB | $0.07 |
| Resources set explicitly, for example | 8 / 32 GiB / 20 GiB | $0.92 |

Set CPU and memory yourself when you create a GPU sandbox. Left at the request defaults, an on-demand H100 costs $3.95 for the GPU plus about $3.97 for CPU, memory and disk, if Daytona bills them on top the way its billing docs describe.

results.title: GPU Sandbox Pricing: Modal vs Daytona vs Thunder Compute (2026)
results.author: Carl Peterson
highlights:
GPU sandbox pricing compared: an H100 sandbox costs $2.95 to $3.95/hr at Thunder Compute, Modal and Daytona. See full per-second rates and real costs.

Carl Peterson · Updated Nov 05, 2026 · 10 min Read

H100 GPU sandboxes start at $2.95/hr on Thunder Compute and cost up to $3.95/hr on Modal and Daytona's on-demand tier. Daytona also offers cheaper preemptible rates, but sandboxes can be terminated without notice. All three platforms charge separately for vCPUs and memory; GPU rates are only part of the bill.

This guide breaks down the GPU sandbox bill and the rules that affect the total. Base prices were last reviewed in October 2026, before volume discounts or region multipliers.

...

Daytona preemptible sandboxes have the lowest hourly rate if runs survive. Evicted runs must be paid for again. At base rates, Thunder Compute is about 20% cheaper than Daytona on-demand and 27% cheaper than Modal for this configuration.

## GPU Rates for Other GPUs on Modal and Daytona

Modal and Daytona charge identical rates for every GPU but under different conditions: Daytona's GPU sandboxes are on-demand, and Modal's are preemptible.

### Daytona Sandbox Pricing: On-Demand vs Preemptible

Daytona's preemptible GPU rate is about 42% lower than its on-demand rate for every GPU. A Daytona H100 costs $3.95/hr on-demand and $2.27/hr preemptible. Preemptible sandboxes can be terminated without notice, keeping evicted sandboxes retrievable for 24 hours.

Daytona tiers also behave differently when GPUs are out of stock:

- On-demand requests wait until capacity frees up.
- Preemptible requests fail immediately.

vCPU, memory and storage cost the same on both Daytona tiers.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

The L40S held, the first card Verda has left flat on a rise day in this run. The same morning, Lambda announced rises of about 15% for Nov 16.

...

What changed, read on verda.com/pricing on Nov 6, 2026 (unrounded page figures in brackets): GB300 $13.31 → $13.44 [$13.44], B300 $11.57 → $11.69 [$11.69], B200 $9.05 → $9.14 [$9.138], H200 $6.38 → $6.44 [$6.440], H100 SXM $4.89 → $4.94 [$4.938], A100 80GB $2.29 → $2.32 [$2.316], A100 40GB $1.64 → $1.66 [$1.657] and RTX PRO 6000 $2.70 → $2.73 [$2.725]. The L40S held at $1.94 [$1.939]. Each rise is within a whisker of +1.0% — the same uniform list adjustment as the nine before it.

The pattern: Verda rose on Oct 23, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30,

...

What it costs: Verda holds the board's Best offer on only two cards — the GB300 and the A100 40GB — and both rose today, so those two best offers rose with it. Everywhere else the cheapest verified offers are other providers' and none moved: the board's H100 SXM best is still TensorDock at $2.25 an hour (at an 8-GPU minimum) and its B200 best is still RunPod Community at $5.98. If you rent at Verda around the clock, today's rise adds about $95 a month per GB300, $66 per B200 and $36 per H100 on a 730-hour month.

How much does a GPU cost per hour at GPUwithCrypto?

An H100 80GB costs $2.32/hour at GPUwithCrypto, an A100 80GB $0.92/hour and an RTX 4090 $0.28/hour, billed per minute and paid in crypto with no KYC. On 13 November 2026, these prices were below the mean on-demand price of 5 rivals on 7 of 7 GPUs; marketplace and community offers were lower on 5.

- Sold as blocks of GPU-hours (10, 24, 168 or 720 hours of one GPU model), used per minute while an instance runs; unused hours do not expire.
- Paid in crypto only (BTC, USDT, USDC, ETH, SOL, LTC, XMR) from a prepaid balance, minimum top-up $25; the sending wallet pays the network fee and GPUwithCrypto adds none.
- Against on-demand list prices (13 November 2026): from −20% (L40S) to −58% (RTX 4090) under the mean of Massed Compute, Thunder Compute, RunPod, Lambda and Salad.

results.title: GPU Rental Price Report, November 2026 · EverXCloud
highlights:
Public GPU-hour prices for H100, H200, B200, A100, L40S, RTX 4090 and RTX 5090 across 16 cloud providers, with medians and spreads.

## Executive summary

EverXCloud read the public pricing pages of 16 GPU cloud providers on 2026-10-26 and recorded 75 prices per GPU-hour for eight GPUs. On-demand prices for the same GPU still vary widely between providers, and spot, preemptible or community capacity costs far less than on-demand capacity.

This report covers third-party list prices only. Once the EverXCloud Marketplace launches, its own price index will be published from real transactions.

## Key findings

1. The median on-demand H100 SXM price across 11 providers is $3.99 per GPU-hour, from $3.14 to $6.16: the most expensive listing costs 2.0× the cheapest.
2. Spot, preemptible and community H100 SXM capacity has a median of $2.30 per GPU-hour across 3 providers, 42% below the on-demand median.
3. The H200 carries a 24% premium over the H100 SXM at the median ($4.94 vs $3.99 on demand, 10 providers).
4. On-demand B200 prices range from $6.00 to $8.60 per GPU-hour across 7 providers, with a median of $8.19.
5. The A100 80GB shows the widest relative spread among data center GPUs: 2.6× between the cheapest ($1.09) and the most expensive ($2.79) on-demand listing, across 9 providers.
6. AWS Capacity Blocks, a short-term reservation, list the H100 at $5.97 and the B200 at $14.21 per GPU-hour, 1.5× and 1.7× the on-demand medians of the other providers.

- Prices were read on 2026-10-26 on each provider's official public pricing page, in USD per GPU-hour, excluding tax. No price was estimated, negotiated or taken from a third-party aggregator.
- One price per provider, GPU and offer type. When a provider lists several configurations for the same GPU, the lowest listed price was kept, and the listing is recorded in the data.
- Multi-GPU instances are converted to a per-GPU price by dividing the instance price by the number of GPUs (for example CoreWeave and AWS 8-GPU instances).
- On-demand and spot, preemptible or community prices are reported separately. AWS prices are Capacity Block rates, a short-term reservation, and are not included in the on-demand statistics.

- The median of an even number of prices is the mean of the two middle values.

highlights:
## What does it cost per hour to rent an H100 in 2026?

As of November 2026, H100 SXM listings on marketplace providers generally sit around $2.00-$3.50 per GPU per hour on-demand, with spot instances landing nearer $1.20-$2.20.

That is the normalized range across public listings I have been tracking. The nvidia h100 hourly price swings hard by provider, region, and whether you are looking at a single GPU or an 8-GPU node, multi-GPU nodes usually price lower per GPU but force you to take the whole box.

Here is roughly how the common models shake out. Read these as ranges, not quotes; they move every few days.
